response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT o.orderbase AS ch, f.feerate AS r FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS oa FROM j), chan AS (SELECT ch, AVG(r) AS ca FROM j WHERE ch IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ch) SELECT AVG(chan.ca) AS mean_channel_avg_fee_rate, AVG(chan.ca - overall.oa) AS mean_excess_over_overall_avg FROM chan, overall WHERE chan.ca > overall.oa

assumptions.assumption: The 'average' benchmark is the overall mean feerate across all fee rows linked to an order (not the mean of the channel means). Each channel's average is the mean of its fee rows' feerate.
Fees with no matching order are excluded (inner join), null feerates are ignored, and orders with a null orderbase are not counted as a channel.

alternatives.interpretation: The benchmark is the mean of the per-channel average fee rates, so each channel counts equally, instead of the mean over fee rows.
alternatives.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT o.orderbase AS ch, f.feerate AS r FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL), chan AS (SELECT ch, AVG(r) AS ca FROM j GROUP BY ch), overall AS (SELECT AVG(ca) AS oa FROM chan) SELECT AVG(chan.ca) AS mean_channel_avg_fee_rate, AVG(chan.ca - overall.oa) AS mean_excess_over_overall_avg FROM chan, overall WHERE chan.ca > overall.oa
